questions.question: In story S10 (Invite-context rumor (D3): send, hold, validate, view model), is there any vacuous or placeholder production path: a no-op/stub body, a tautological assertion, a frozen stand-in constant, or an optional dependency (injected port, handler, client handle) that silently degrades to non-behavior when not injected? Cite file:line for each injection point in app/src/lib/marmot/invitations/inviteContext.ts; app/src/lib/marmot/invitations/inviteContextStore.ts; app/src/lib/marmot/invitations/inviteContextHandler.ts; app/src/lib/marmot/invitations/invitationCardViewModel.ts; app/src/components/groups/InvitationCard.tsx (view-model consumption only); app/src/lib/i18n.ts (generic label en+de) and show that omitting the dependency fails loudly rather than succeeding silently.

Could `invitations` be deleted and rewritten without modifying any file outside its `dependencies_allowed` list? If not, which cross-module dependencies exist and do they flow through declared seam contracts in architecture.md (imports only via each module's index.ts, no React-context imports under app/src/lib/marmot/**, no ts-mls or @internet-privacy/marmot-ts imports)?

Does S10 comply with the architecture.md boundary rules: only `client/` constructs or disposes the MarmotClient, code inside HistoryBackend calls / inbox handlers / client listeners never awaits an account-scope client call (follow-up work via the owned setTimeout(0) FIFO), group sender identity comes only from orderingKey.account, and idb-keyval update() is not used? List each rule touched by this story's files with file:line evidence, or state why it is not touched.

Do unit, property, and (where the AC names them) library-harness or e2e tests cover the artifacts named in S10's scope (app/src/lib/marmot/invitations/inviteContext.ts; app/src/lib/marmot/invitations/inviteContextStore.ts; app/src/lib/marmot/invitations/inviteContextHandler.ts; app/src/lib/marmot/invitations/invitationCardViewModel.ts; app/src/components/groups/InvitationCard.tsx (view-model consumption only); app/src/lib/i18n.ts (generic label en+de))? Show that tests use real collaborators or test fixtures rather than mocking the helper used at the SUT call site, that idb mocks are seeded out of key order where order matters, and that at least one test fails if the production code is replaced by a no-op.

Does the delivered S10 implementation match the intent of its scope (Sponsor sends kind-21064 {groupId,name} via sendInboxRumor after delivered/retryable; invitee inbox handler (registerInboxHandler) dedupes by rumor.id, holds contexts under 8/sender, 64 total, 7 days, validates against sponsorAccount/sponsors, deletes on accept/decline/expiry; pure card view model () and respect its exclusions (groups-invitation-preview e2e rewrite (S26))? Identify any capability owned by a later story that was built ahead, or any in-scope capability left unimplemented.

Which trust or validation boundaries does S10 touch (signer budget/permissions, relay-supplied events, rumor sender/pubkey attribution, invite/join payloads, privacy invariant that no profile metadata is published to public relays)? Show the validation or defensive check at each boundary with file:line evidence and a test that feeds a malformed or hostile input and observes rejection.

AC-CTX-1: After a `delivered`/`retryable` invite outcome, the sponsor MUST send one `extensions.sendInboxRumor` of kind 21064 with content exactly `{"groupId":<id>,"name":<name>}` (no other keys, no description, no admins, no profile data); a `failed` outcome MUST send none. Provide evidence of (a) the production code satisfying this (file:line), (b) the test(s) at level [unit (recording sendInboxRumor)] that exercise it end-to-end and would fail for a stub/no-op, and (c) confirmation that those tests are not pure mock-spy proxies.

AC-CTX-2: The invitation card MUST show the context's group name only when the context `rumor.pubkey` equals the invitation's `sponsorAccount` or one of its `sponsors`; any other sender MUST yield the generic label. The stored name MUST be keyed by `groupId+sponsor`, length-capped (cap constant asserted), and rendered as untrusted text (a name of `x` renders as literal text in the view model). The card MUST update live whether the context or the invitation arrives first, and MUST show the generic label when no context arrived. Provide evidence of (a) the production code satisfying this (file:line), (b) the test(s) at level [unit (pure view-model function) + e2e:groups-invitation-preview (rewritten)] that exercise it end-to-end and would fail for a stub/no-op, and (c) confirmation that those tests are not pure mock-spy proxies.

AC-CTX-3: Holding store: contexts with no matching invitation MUST be kept at most 8 per sender and 64 in total (oldest evicted first), and expire after 7 days (fake-time). A held context MUST be validated against `sponsorAccount` when the invitation arrives and dropped on mismatch. The stored context MUST be deleted on accept, decline and expiry (7 days or the invitation leaving `invitations.pending()`). Tests assert exact retained sets after inserting 9/65 entries, and after 7 days + 1 ms. Provide evidence of (a) the production code satisfying this (file:line), (b) the test(s) at level [unit] that exercise it end-to-end and would fail for a stub/no-op, and (c) confirmation that those tests are not pure mock-spy proxies.

AC-CTX-4: The invite-context handler MUST dedupe by `rumor.id` (redelivery stores one entry) and MUST persist-and-return without calling any account-scope client method. Provide evidence of (a) the production code satisfying this (file:line), (b) the test(s) at level [unit] that exercise it end-to-end and would fail for a stub/no-op, and (c) confirmation that those tests are not pure mock-spy proxies.

AC-CTX-5: The invitation card MUST never show description or admin list pre-join. Provide evidence of (a) the production code satisfying this (file:line), (b) the test(s) at level [unit (view model contains no such fields); e2e:groups-invitation-preview (rewritten)] that exercise it end-to-end and would fail for a stub/no-op, and (c) confirmation that those tests are not pure mock-spy proxies.

In app/src/lib/marmot/inviteContextIdbPort.ts the IndexedDB adapter lives outside app/src/lib/marmot/invitations/ (the S9 structural scan in pendingView.test.ts forbids idb-keyval inside that directory). Confirm the store itself (inviteContextStore.ts) cannot silently run without persistence: createInviteContextStore throws TypeError at construction when port.load/port.save are missing, and a failing save is reported through onError while memory keeps serving the card. Cite the tests.

Hostile-input boundary of the invite-context handler (inviteContextHandler.ts): the sender is only the seal-bound rumor.pubkey (lowercased, 64-hex checked), a blocked sender is dropped before store.add, payload extras (description, admins, profile data) are never carried into the stored record, the name is sanitised/capped (sanitizeContextName, 64 code points, control and bidi characters removed), and a non-sponsor context for a pending group is dropped on add and on reconcile. Show the tests that feed each hostile shape and observe rejection.

Re-entrancy: the inviteContext inbox handler awaits only store.add (app storage, no MarmotClient call) and enqueues nothing; reconcile/discard run from view.onChange and UI action decorators, outside library frames. The sender (createInviteContextSender) calls extensions.sendInboxRumor and must therefore only be invoked from a UI handler or queued job. Is there any call path where S12 or the UI wiring could invoke createContextSendingInviter from inside a library frame? Name the call sites and the guard (the library rejects 'reentrant').

Wiring left for later stories: the production composition (registering createInviteContextHandler as inboxHandlers.inviteContext in the bootstrap, binding the store to the pending view after seed with bindInviteContextToPendingView, switching InvitationCard consumers to pass viewModel, replacing the invite call site with createContextSendingInviter) is NOT done in S10 (the legacy MarmotContext cut-over is S22). Verify nothing in S10 claims this wiring and that InvitationCard falls back to the legacy Welcome decode when no viewModel is passed.

inviteContext.harness.test.ts drives REAL clients (FakeRelay, bootstrapAccountClient, real sendInboxRumor and inbox handler registration). Confirm: exactly one extra kind-1059 wrap carries the context, no kind-21064 event is stored at top level and the group name never appears in any stored relay event (AC-PRIV-2), a failed invite publishes no wrap, a non-sponsor context for the same group is dropped, a blocked sponsor's context is dropped with a positive control showing the same wrap is stored once unblocked.
